subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the median of a set of data?
options: The middle value when the data is arranged in order
The value that occurs most often
The difference between the highest and lowest values
The sum of the values divided by how many there are
questions.explain: The median is the middle value once the data has been placed in ascending or descending order.

questions.q: The mode of a set of data is best described as:
options: The value that occurs most often
The mean of the largest and smallest values
questions.explain: The mode is the most frequently occurring value in a data set.

questions.q: How is the range of a set of data calculated?
options: Total of the values divided by their number
questions.explain: The range measures spread and equals the largest value minus the smallest value.

questions.q: On the probability scale, all probabilities take values between:
questions.explain: A probability is always a number from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).

questions.q: For a complete set of mutually exclusive outcomes, the probabilities of all the outcomes add up to:
questions.explain: The probabilities of an exhaustive set of mutually exclusive events sum to 1.

questions.q: On a histogram with unequal class widths, what is plotted on the vertical axis?
questions.explain: Histograms with unequal class widths use frequency density on the vertical axis so that area represents frequency.

questions.q: The angles in a pie chart must add up to a total of:
questions.explain: A pie chart is a full circle, so the sector angles total 360°.

questions.q: The interquartile range (IQR) is found by calculating:
questions.explain: The IQR = Q3 - Q1 and measures the spread of the middle 50% of the data.

questions.q: To find the probability that two independent events both happen, you should:
questions.explain: For independent events, P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B).

questions.q: How is frequency density calculated for a histogram bar?
questions.explain: Frequency density = frequency ÷ class width, so the bar's area equals its frequency.

questions.q: If the probability of an event A is P(A), the probability that A does NOT happen is:
questions.explain: The probability of an event not occurring is 1 minus the probability that it does.

questions.q: When estimating the mean from a grouped frequency table, which value represents each class?
questions.explain: Each class is represented by its midpoint, which is multiplied by the frequency to estimate the mean.

questions.q: A scatter graph shows that as one variable increases the other decreases. This shows:
questions.explain: When one quantity rises as the other falls, the scatter graph shows negative correlation.

questions.q: On a cumulative frequency graph for n data values, the median is read off at a cumulative frequency of:
questions.explain: The median corresponds to the value at half the total cumulative frequency, n/2.

questions.q: Find the mean of the data set: 4, 7, 9, 10, 10.
questions.explain: The values total 40 and there are 5 of them, so the mean is 40 ÷ 5 = 8.

questions.q: Find the median of the data set: 3, 5, 8, 9, 12, 15.
questions.explain: With six ordered values the median is the mean of the middle two: (8 + 9) ÷ 2 = 8.5.

questions.q: A bag contains 3 red, 5 blue and 2 green counters. One counter is taken at random. What is the probability it is red?
questions.explain: There are 10 counters in total, so P(red) = 3 ÷ 10 = 0.3.

questions.q: On a histogram a bar has a frequency density of 4 and a class width of 5. What is the frequency for that class?
